subject: Acceptance orchestra + exit-test manifest for Novamed pilot
messages:
From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: Holly Price <hprice@novamed.com>, Carlos Vega <cvega@novamed.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acceptance orchestra + exit-test manifest for Novamed pilot

Hi Holly / Carlos —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, attached is a first-pass acceptance manifest and a short catalog of verification tests we propose to use during the 6-week evaluation. The purpose of this thread is to lock the exit gates (what passes), the acceptance tests (how we verify), and the owners/timeline so procurement and your engineering team can align with our CS handoff.

High-level summary (see attached acceptance-manifest-v1.xlsx):
- Success criteria: 1) 95% endpoint availability during normal business hours (PST) over a 2-week stretch; 2) Conversational accuracy: >= 85% on the supplied clinical QA set; 3) Latency: p50 < 220ms, p95 < 750ms for single-turn queries under baseline load.
- Exit gates (all required to reach buy signal):
  * Safety & privacy review complete (data handling checklist signed) — owner: Novamed security / markus for evidence collection
  * SLA smoke: availability & latency thresholds met for 10 consecutive business days — owner: laura
  * Quality run: pass >= 85% on the clinical QA vignettes and no high-severity hallucination cases in sampling — owner: marissa
  * Operational runbook vetted and can reproduce key flows end-to-end — owner: Novamed dev lead (Carlos)
- Acceptance tests (examples in test-vignettes.pdf):
  * End-to-end sample replay: 200 sample patient prompts -> verify response correctness, redaction, and format (automated scoring + manual spot-checking).
  * Load smoke: 50 qps for 15 minutes to observe latency distribution.
  * Failover exercise: simulate endpoint degradation and confirm fallback to backup model within 60s.

Proposed timeline (dates are placeholders we can firm up):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize manifest & sign evidence checklist (target 9/10)
- Weeks 1–2: integration + baseline functional verification (automated tests)
- Weeks 3–4: quality validation with clinical vignettes + user-acceptance sampling
- Week 5: SLA smoke and operational runbook validation
- Week 6: close decision and handoff (target decision meeting 9/18)

Attachments: acceptance-manifest-v1.xlsx, test-vignettes.pdf. I can update the workbook to add the latency budgets and data-retention column if you want — flagged as action item 1 below.

Action items today:
1) Holly/Carlos: confirm the Novamed security contact for the data-handling checklist and whether the QA set provided earlier is the canonical one (reply inline)
2) Novamed dev: nominate one owner for the operational runbook validation (name + email)
3) Redwood: we'll add explicit latency budgets and the DOCS link to the manifest and share an updated workbook by EOD 9/7

Thanks — looking forward to locking these gates so the evaluation has a clean pass/fail definition.

—
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): acceptance-manifest-v1.xlsx (workbook), test-vignettes.pdf (sample vignettes)

From: Holly Price <hprice@novamed.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: Carlos Vega <cvega@novamed.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acceptance orchestra + exit-test manifest for Novamed pilot

Markus —

Appreciate the clear draft. A few clarifying items from our side before we sign: 

1) Latency budgets — can you split p95 targets by model variant (full context vs trimmed context)? For our workflows the p95 for large-context sessions is more forgiving.
2) Data retention & logging — we need explicit language about what traces are retained during the eval (KV cache, prompt text, derived embeddings) and for how long. This ties into our privacy team sign-off.
3) Acceptance evidence — will you provide a CSV of the automated scoring results and the sampling notes for any manual spot checks? We need that for procurement and audit.

Also: Carlos will own the operational runbook validation. I'll loop in procurement (procure@novamed.com) separately for the contract-related timing.

If you can incorporate the two items above and send an updated manifest by EOD today, we should be able to confirm the security contact and sign the checklist by 9/10.

Thanks,
Holly
Holly Price
Director, Clinical AI Programs
Novamed

Changes made based on your asks:
- Split latency budgets: p50/p95 for full-context (p50<320ms, p95<900ms) and trimmed-context (p50<200ms, p95<650ms).
- Trace retention row added: default 30 days; option to extend to 90 days with an approved request (listed procedure & KMS note).
- Evidence bundle: we'll export automated scoring as CSV and include a manual-spotcheck log (location in Drive).
- SLA smoke & failover runbook: laura has drafted the checklist; I'll attach the runbook PDF to the manifest by EOD 9/9.

Next steps / commitments:
- 9/10: Novamed security confirms contact & signs data-handling checklist
- 9/10–9/23: Integration + verification windows per the manifest
- 9/24: SLA smoke & operational runbook validation window
- 9/25: Decision meeting (go/no-go) — calendar invite to follow from procurement

Carlos — thank you for owning the operational runbook validation; please confirm the dev lead's email so we can add them to the verification tasks. Holly — once procurement confirms the calendar invite I'll lock the timeline.

If that all looks good I'll mark the manifest version as v1.1 (attachments updated) and move to evidence collection.
